messages:
sara.dev: quick heads-up — ran int8 reranker onboarding against the new candidate pool 'pool_v3'. NDCG@10 vs baseline is flat (+0.2) but MRR@10 drops ~6% on the synthetic-paraphrase slice. Thoughts?

pranav.ml: did you run with the same tokenization/normalization? small differences can blow up MRR on short queries.

sara.dev: yes same tokenizer v2, canonical normalization on both. I suspect candidate ordering shift from paraphrase variants. added results attached (excerpt):

sara.dev: ```
# eval command
python eval_rerank.py --model rerank-int8-v5 --candidates pool_v3 --slice paraphrase_synth
# metrics
NDCG@10: 0.423 (baseline 0.421)
MRR@10: 0.297 (baseline 0.316)
``` 

kai-research: could be sample mismatch in how negatives were constructed. Are paraphrase negatives present in baseline's candidate set? If baseline had stronger negatives that pushed paraphrase positives up, calibration changes post-quant.

eva-ops: also check whether KV cache alignment/packing changed after INT8 kernel switch — tiny softmax scale shifts can reorder close-scoring items.

pranav.ml: quick repro plan: 1) rerun eval with deterministic seed + same candidate pool 2) run float16/float32 on same infra to isolate quant effect 3) construct minimal synthetic case with 1 query + paraphrase variants to observe score deltas.

sara.dev: starting 1 & 2 now. adding small synthetic test. pinging @eval-bot to create reproducible job.

eval-bot: created job eval/2789123456-paraphrase-repro. logs: https://ci.example.com/2789123456

kai-research: if we see consistent rank swaps, we should add a small calibration/scaling sweep in the onboarding CI (scale in [0.98,1.02]) — quick PR in the harness could catch this early.

sara.dev: agreed. I'll add a CI job and a short writeup on the onboarding checklist.

pranav.ml: one more ask: record per-query score deltas, not just metrics. that'll tell whether it's a broad shift or a few outliers.

sara.dev: will do. thanks.
